<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 1 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Wonderful Wizard of Oz ==

Aunt Em is the wife of Uncle Henry, a farmer, and Dorothy's aunt. She lives with him on the Kansas prairies, in a small house built from lumber hauled by wagon over many miles — a single room holding a cookstove, a cupboard, a table, a few chairs, and the beds, along with a dug-out cyclone cellar where the family could shelter from the great whirlwinds that could crush the building. When Aunt Em first came to live there she was a young, pretty wife, but the sun and wind of the prairie changed her over the years, much as they grayed the house and the land around it.

Throughout Dorothy's time away, Aunt Em remains constantly in her niece's thoughts: Dorothy repeatedly voices her wish to return to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry, worries that Aunt Em will be dreadfully anxious over her long absence, and fears Aunt Em may believe something terrible has befallen her. When Dorothy finally makes her way home, she finds Aunt Em outside the house watering the cabbages; seeing Dorothy running toward her, Aunt Em calls out, "My darling child!" and welcomes her back.

=== Events ===

* Dorothy lives with Uncle Henry and Aunt Em in a small house on the gray Kansas prairies.
* Uncle Henry spots an approaching cyclone, warns Aunt Em, and runs to secure the livestock.
* Aunt Em orders Dorothy to the storm cellar and climbs down first while Dorothy searches for Toto.
* The four companions meet in the Throne Room; the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, and Lion each express contentment with what they gained from Oz, but Dorothy insists she wants to return to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry in Kansas.
* Dorothy recounts her whole story to Glinda and says her greatest wish is to return to Kansas to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry.
* Aunt Em is watering the cabbages outside the house when she sees Dorothy running toward her.
* Aunt Em cries out and embraces Dorothy, kissing her face and asking where she came from.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 3 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== Ozma of Oz / A Record of Her Adventures with Dorothy Gale of Kansas, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, the Cowardly Lion, and the Hungry Tiger; Besides Other Good People too Numerous to Mention Faithfully Recorded Herein ==

Aunt Em lives at the old Kansas farm together with Uncle Henry. When Dorothy wishes to see the farm, a vision shows Aunt Em there, washing dishes by the kitchen window, and she seems quite well and contented. While trapped as an ornament in the Nome King's palace, Dorothy wonders whether Uncle Henry or Aunt Em will ever learn what has become of her.

=== Events ===

* Dorothy uses Ozma's magic picture to check on Aunt Em (well and content) and Uncle Henry (in Australia, sad and unwell) and decides she must return to him.
</div>
<div class="mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" data-expandtext="Book 6 — reveal" data-collapsetext="Hide">
== The Emerald City of Oz ==

Aunt Em travels with Dorothy, Uncle Henry, and the Wizard through the Land of Oz, encountering many oddities she does not fully understand. Skeptical of unfamiliar things, she remarks that "no one would suspect it from their name" upon hearing of an unfamiliar group, and later wonders whether they are "more paper things." When a kangaroo cries inconsolably, she suggests "it must be her mince-pie," a guess Uncle Henry answers with his own, "or her milk-toast." Invited to lunch with the Tin Woodman, she asks with some apprehension, "Must we lunch on tin?", and Dorothy reassures her that Nick Chopper will provide "plenty of good things to eat." At the Tin Woodman's castle she remains wary of local hazards, inquiring whether he keeps "any Flutterbudgets or Rigmaroles," and comments dryly on the castle's spotless tin surfaces, supposing "they polish their Emperor, too."

=== Events ===

* Dorothy tells the group she is not hungry, having eaten a wheelbarrow and a piano and lunched with a King, prompting disbelief from Aunt Em.
* Dorothy recounts her day's adventures to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry, including her visits to Utensia, Bunbury, and Bunnybury.
</div>
